findings.claim: task4 tampers the token by replacing its last two characters ('xx', or 'yy' when it already ends in 'xx'). The last base64url character of a 43-character HS256 signature carries only 4 significant bits, and Nimbus decodes leniently, so when a token happens to end in 'xw' the replacement 'xx' decodes to the byte-identical signature ('w'=110000 and 'x'=110001 differ only in the 2 discarded trailing bits): the 'tampered' token is then still valid and the expected 401 becomes 200. Tokens vary per run via issuedAt, so this is a genuine (if rare, roughly 1 in 1024 runs) flake in which a fully correct implementation fails.
findings.recommendation: Tamper a fully significant position instead, e.g. flip a character in the middle of the payload (second JWT segment) or in the middle of the signature, or append an extra character; any of these always invalidates the signature.
